title: Static synchronized vs instance synchronized: different locks, can run simultaneously
shortTitle: What is static vs instance synchronized?
keyPoints: A static synchronized method locks on the Class object (ClassName.class), shared by all instances.
An instance synchronized method locks on this, the specific object instance.
These are two different locks, so a static and an instance synchronized method can run simultaneously.
Two instance synchronized methods on the same object share the same this lock and block each other.
Two instance synchronized methods on different objects have different this locks and run in parallel.
If both must be mutually exclusive, use a shared static final lock object explicitly.

s1_definition.oneliner: Static synchronized locks on the Class object while instance synchronized locks on this, and because they are different locks, they can execute simultaneously.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Static synchronized** – `public static synchronized void audit()` locks on `ClassName.class`. This is one lock shared by all instances of the class.
- **Instance synchronized** – `public synchronized void debit()` locks on `this`, the specific object instance. Each instance has its own lock.
- **Different locks** – because the Class object and `this` are different objects, a static synchronized method and an instance synchronized method can run at the same time on the same object.
- **Same lock** – two instance synchronized methods called on the same object use the same `this` lock and block each other. Two instance synchronized methods called on different objects use different `this` locks and run in parallel.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank has two padlocks: one on the main vault door (Class lock, shared by all branches) and one on Rajesh's personal drawer (instance lock, specific to Rajesh's account). A teller locking the vault door does not prevent another teller from opening Rajesh's drawer because they are different padlocks. Only when two tellers try to use the same padlock does one have to wait.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Lock Objects:

  ┌──────────────────────────┐
  │ AccountService.class      │ ◀── static synchronized methods lock here
  │ (ONE per class in JVM)    │
  └──────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────────┐
  │ instance1 (this)          │   │ instance2 (this)          │
  │ debit() locks here        │   │ debit() locks here        │
  └──────────────────────────┘   └──────────────────────────┘
  ◀── instance synchronized        ◀── different lock: parallel!
       methods lock here

  Static sync + Instance sync = DIFFERENT locks = PARALLEL
  Instance sync (obj1) + Instance sync (obj2) = DIFFERENT locks = PARALLEL
  Instance sync (obj1) + Instance sync (obj1) = SAME lock = BLOCKED
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A static synchronized method locks on the Class object, while an instance synchronized method locks on `this`. These are different lock objects, so they can execute simultaneously. This surprises developers who expect all synchronized methods to be mutually exclusive. They are only mutually exclusive when they share the same lock.

The practical implication: if your globalAudit() (static synchronized) needs to prevent debits (instance synchronized) during the report, both must use the same lock object. The default Class-vs-this separation will not help. Use a `private static final Object SHARED_LOCK` and synchronize both methods on it.

Remember one sentence: static synchronized locks on the Class object, instance synchronized locks on this, and because they are different locks, they can run in parallel.
